blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate

  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per

  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated

messages.preview: The failure is a test bug of mine: `args.take(4)` vs a 3-element expected list — the inner `expect` throws inside the runner, which the production catch correctly converts to `PasteboardUnavailable`. …

blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

The failure is a test bug of mine: `args.take(4)` vs a 3-element expected list — the inner `expect` throws inside the runner, which the production catch correctly converts to `PasteboardUnavailable`. Fix the test:

{"newText":"      expect(exe, 'sips');\n      expect(args.take(3), ['-s', 'format', 'png']);","oldText":"      expect(exe, 'sips');\n      expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']);","path":"test/cli/clipboard_reader_test.dart"}

- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate

  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per

  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,

blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

The failure is a test bug of mine: `args.take(4)` vs a 3-element expected list — the inner `expect` throws inside the runner, which the production catch correctly converts to `PasteboardUnavailable`. Fix the test:

  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).

  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated

  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final

  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;

blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

The failure is a test bug of mine: `args.take(4)` vs a 3-element expected list — the inner `expect` throws inside the runner, which the production catch correctly converts to `PasteboardUnavailable`. Fix the test:

blocks.text:
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate

wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated

blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

The failure is a test bug of mine: `args.take(4)` vs a 3-element expected list — the inner `expect` throws inside the runner, which the production catch correctly converts to `PasteboardUnavailable`. Fix the test:

- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate

  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per

  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,

messages.preview: The failure is a test bug of mine: `args.take(4)` vs a 3-element expected list — the inner `expect` throws inside the runner, which the production catch correctly converts to `PasteboardUnavailable`. …

blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

The failure is a test bug of mine: `args.take(4)` vs a 3-element expected list — the inner `expect` throws inside the runner, which the production catch correctly converts to `PasteboardUnavailable`. Fix the test:

blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

The failure is a test bug of mine: `args.take(4)` vs a 3-element expected list — the inner `expect` throws inside the runner, which the production catch correctly converts to `PasteboardUnavailable`. Fix the test:

  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,

One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. - Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate

blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate

blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

messages.preview: The failure is a test bug of mine: `args.take(4)` vs a 3-element expected list — the inner `expect` throws inside the runner, which the production catch correctly converts to `PasteboardUnavailable`. …

blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

The failure is a test bug of mine: `args.take(4)` vs a 3-element expected list — the inner `expect` throws inside the runner, which the production catch correctly converts to `PasteboardUnavailable`. Fix the test:

  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate

- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate

blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,

blocks.text:
One failure: 'a TIFF-only macOS pasteboard converts to PNG via sips' got `PasteboardUnavailable` instead of `PasteboardImage`. Why?

Look at the flow: PNGf probe → rc=1 → JPEG probe → rc=1 → TIFF probe → rc=0 writes tiff bytes → `_convertTiffToPng`: writes tiffPath, runs sips, sips writes png, rc=0 → `File(pngPath).readAsBytesSync()` → return png bytes → PasteboardImage.

Hmm, but the fake runner in the test: for `sips`, the test asserts `args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png']` then writes PNG to `args[indexOf('--out')+1]` and returns `_ok(const [])`.

Wait — why unavailable? Let me think... In the test's runner, `expect(exe, 'sips')` — if an assertion inside the runner throws... no wait, that would fail the test with that error, not PasteboardUnavailable. Actually — exceptions inside the runner are caught by `_readPlatform`'s `on Object catch` → returns `PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')`. That's what happened! The `expect` inside the runner threw (or something else), got swallowed by the catch, and became PasteboardUnavailable.

What could throw? `args.take(4)` equals `['-s','format','png']`... wait, `expect(args.take(4), ['-s', 'format', 'png'])` — take(4) gives 4 elements but the expected list has 3! `-s format png <tiffPath> --out <pngPath>` → take(4) = ['-s','format','png', tiffPath] ≠ ['-s','format','png']. That's my test bug — should be take(3).

Also the failure message printed the final assertion instead of the inner one (the inner one became PasteboardUnavailable('pasteboard read failed: ...')). Fix: take(3).

The failure is a test bug of mine: `args.take(4)` vs a 3-element expected list — the inner `expect` throws inside the runner, which the production catch correctly converts to `PasteboardUnavailable`. Fix the test:

- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

- `_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»` and `«class JPEG»`; a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`.
- Ctrl+V fired only the image probe and returned — a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all, so the keystroke did nothing but print the probe's error.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` into a scratch file and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output is returned as `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through, scratch files always cleaned up.
- Same file: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner` / `platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable. Windows strips the one formatter newline.
- `paste_image.dart`: new pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → text inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. `readClipboardText` callback added to `FaTuiCallbacks` (real + web stub) and wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS pasteboard → sips output used; failed conversion → `PasteboardUnavailable`; `readPasteboardText` per-platform tests (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip, failure naming).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts into the composer; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: PENDING.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics are unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.
- `clipboard_reader.dart` stays on the session-deletion unlink allowlist (scratch files in the system temp dir only).

  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»` and `«class JPEG»`; a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` into a scratch file and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output is returned as `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through, scratch files always cleaned up.

- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → text inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. `readClipboardText` callback added to `FaTuiCallbacks` (real + web stub) and wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

- Full suite: PENDING.

- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»` and `«class JPEG»`; a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`.
- Ctrl+V fired only the image probe and returned — a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all, so the keystroke did nothing but print the probe's error.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` into a scratch file and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output is returned as `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through, scratch files always cleaned up.
- Same file: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner` / `platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable. Windows strips the one formatter newline.
- `paste_image.dart`: new pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → text inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. `readClipboardText` callback added to `FaTuiCallbacks` (real + web stub) and wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS pasteboard → sips output used; failed conversion → `PasteboardUnavailable`; `readPasteboardText` per-platform tests (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip, failure naming).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts into the composer; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: PENDING.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics are unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.
- `clipboard_reader.dart` stays on the session-deletion unlink allowlist (scratch files in the system temp dir only).

  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate

- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate

  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,

blocks.text:
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate

- `_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»` and `«class JPEG»`; a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`.
